rumqttc's poll loop reconnects unconditionally — "Continuing to poll will reconnect to the broker if there is a disconnection" — and advertises "Automatic reconnections by just continuing the eventloop.poll()/connection.iter() loop", re-subscription conspicuously absent [[eventloop-in-rumqttc-rust]] [[rumqttc-rust]].

Issue #250, open since February 2021 and still labelled in-pipeline, documents the footgun: after a clean-session reconnect, "I'm not seeing any data coming in from subscribed topics", because subscriptions live only in broker-side session state [[automatic-reconnect-and-subscribed-topics-issue-250-bytebeamiorumqtt-github]].

The in-pipeline fix, PR #1052, is open, unreviewed, v5-scoped, and only emits a reconnect *signal* — its own caller pattern re-subscribes in application code, so subscription ownership stays with the application even if it merges [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].

And the pinned version offers no alternative hook: 0.24.0's `Event` enum has exactly two variants — `Incoming` and `Outgoing`, no `Reconnect` — so `poll()` yielding `Packet::ConnAck` on every connect is the only reconnect signal the pinned version has, making the raw ConnAck match not a workaround but the mandatory design [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].

The queue mechanics are per-client: mosquitto counts each client's queued messages against `max_queued_messages` (default 1000), and for a disconnected client the in-flight adjustment zeroes, freeing the full queue depth for offline replay [[databasec]].

The request-channel capacity of 64 at `agent.rs:62` contradicts rumqttc's recommendation to set capacity 0 when managing pending state — during an outage, up to 64 stale messages queue and replay as a burst [[rumqttrumqttcsrceventlooprs-at-main-bytebeamiorumqtt-github]].

Worse is starvation: `backend-syncthing` builds its reqwest client with no timeout (reqwest has none by default), and `Agent::run` polls all backends sequentially in one task, so one hung syncthing daemon freezes every sensor while availability still reads "online" — sensors that lie rather than sensors that vanish, the worst failure class a fleet can carry [[interim-report-mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec]].

On every `ConnAck` — first connect or reconnect, either `session_present` — re-issue all command-topic subscribes (idempotent; subscribe-before-connect is safe because requests buffer in the bounded channel until post-ConnAck) and re-assert retained "online" [[rumqttrumqttcsrceventlooprs-at-main-bytebeamiorumqtt-github]].

First, `clean_session = true` (explicit, stable client id) against the persistent-session instinct: a persistent session's only unique deliverable here is broker-side queueing of QoS 1 commands for an offline agent, and the kiosks power off overnight — a week-old launcher toggle or reboot replaying as fresh on Monday boot, with no TTL in v3.1.1 (issue #211, open and stale since December 2020) and no payload timestamp to age it by, is a hazard no source states directly but the overnight-off pattern and rumqtt's documented lack of any pending-message TTL jointly imply [[rumqttc-reconnection-to-mqtt-broker-and-pending-messages-ttl-issue-211-bytebeami]].

Second, a premise correction that strengthens the design: 0.24.0 is *not* v3.1.1-locked — `src/lib.rs:113` declares `pub mod v5;` with full property support inside the pinned version, and the module is not a stubbed half-implementation: its single `unimplemented!()` sits on request variants (PubComp/SubAck/UnsubAck/PingResp) the public client never sends — unreachable from agent code — so message and session expiry are a module switch away, a named future option rather than the reason for any workaround [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].

The 0.25.1 upgrade was actually run — check, test, clippy all exit 0, zero code changes — and reverted, because it buys nothing the supervisor needs; the identical public API across the two versions is itself evidence the bump is cosmetic [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].

**Verified ZFS status (europa only).** The procfs-state plus zedlet two-channel design, with the premise correction that scopes it: pallene is ZFS-less and callisto's only ZFS exposure is the iSCSI zvol with no local pool, where the backend's `detect()` already returns false — correct today [[interim-report-headless-privilege-ladder]] [[repo-map-ha-linux-agent]].

**Mesh/exit-node health (europa, fleet visibility).** The tailscale `ipnstate` schema is the surface for peer and exit-node state — PeerStatus with HostName, Online, and ExitNodeStatus for the current exit node's liveness [[ipnstate-package-tailscalecomipnipnstate-go-packages]].

The schema is authoritative but explicitly unstable-by-policy across versions, so the parser is version-tolerant; the operational surface around it — `tailscale wait` / tailscale-online.target as the readiness gate where mesh reachability orders the agent, `BackendState` as the reliable running-indicator, and the frozen-by-policy `--json` contract that makes version-tolerance a schema check rather than a re-parse — completes the feature the same way SMART and ZFS get their mechanisms named [[how-to-check-if-tailscale-is-running-alexwlchan]].

The corpus still fixes the design for the day one is attached, because the HA-native shape is NUT and its ceilings are the agent-side consumer's requirements: the integration cannot talk to a UPS directly (a NUT server is required, port 3493, 60-second default polling), it can retrieve but not set NUT variables and supports no parameterised commands, device actions (instcmds such as beeper.disable, test.battery.start.quick, power-cycle outlet) require credentialled upsd.users grants, it cannot auto-detect a server IP change (DNS-name resolution, never baked IPs), and most diagnostic sensors are disabled by default as a deliberate recorder-cost trim — with `upsc`/`upscmd` enumerating the raw surface an agent-side consumer reads directly [[network-ups-tools-nut-home-assistant]].

**Remote reboot/poweroff.** Present through the launcher and systemd backends [[repo-map-ha-linux-agent]]; what is missing is the idempotency contract — an audit of the fleet's command handlers for non-idempotent semantics (reboot/power among them) is the named next step, because whether any launcher-style command is non-idempotent calibrates how much the clean-session rejection depends on it: if none are, a replayed stale message damages nothing, and the persistence question becomes lower-stakes than the lifecycle design argues.

**CPU performance knobs (kiosks).** The global boost switch lives at `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost` (values 0/1, the recommended interface over the legacy per-policy AMD knob) — a natural governor/EPP sibling for the hardware backend's existing write path, gated by the same udev video-group pattern [[cpu-performance-scaling-the-linux-kernel-documentation]].

**The future desktop host class.** A niri-based desktop host is speculative (niri, a Wayland compositor, appears in zero jupiterOS host configurations), but its boundary is solved from source: the compositor's IPC socket is created as `niri.{wayland_socket_name}.{pid}.sock` under the user's runtime directory — filesystem-permission-gated, so a same-UID `User=io` system service reaches it by globbing, no session unit required (the niri-ipc client library's explicit-path `connect_to()` / `NIRI_SOCKET` being the cleaner reach than globbing) — and the event-stream contract delivers complete state up-front followed by updates, so "your state can never 'desync'" [[serverrs]] [[ipc-niri-msg-niri]] [[niriniri-ipcsrcsocketrs-at-main-niri-wmniri-github]].

The audited fleet facts refute it on arrival: no docker or podman on any jupiterOS host, no container runtime in any host configuration, and the Nix remote builders cannot expose container sockets inside build sandboxes at all — a testcontainers gate would be dead on arrival, not merely awkward [[interim-report-testing-gate-for-hardware-daemon]].

Practice confirms the mechanism on both sides: merged nixpkgs PR #283878 ran a localhost server-client pair inside checkPhase, the build log showing "Serving HTTP on 127.0.0.1 port 8000" serving requests from the test client [[single-file-cli-init-at-1149-by-n8henrie-pull-request-283878-nixosnixpkgs-github]], while the same author's Discourse thread shows the cross-boundary shape failing — a server started outside the build is unreachable from checkPhase because "there are different loopback interfaces in different namespaces", which is precisely why the harness spawns mosquitto inside the test rather than reusing a host broker [[local-networking-in-checkphase-help-nixos-discourse]].

So the mosquitto-subprocess harness inside the test hook — bind a `TcpListener` to `127.0.0.1:0`, read the port, hand it to `mosquitto -p <port>` (the no-config default is anonymous and loopback-only), TCP-probe with a fail-fast, kill on Drop — needs no sandbox escape and no VM [[mosquitto8-mosquitto-debian-unstable-debian-manpages]].
**The seven-step ladder, in dependency order** [[interim-report-testing-gate-for-hardware-daemon]]:

7. **`runNixOSTest` for the module** — the out-of-tree invocation the NixOS manual documents, headless in QEMU where a full system bus and real systemd exist, cribbed from nixpkgs' own mosquitto test with a single node (the kiosk failure mode is local): enable the module, `wait_for_unit("ha-linux-agent.service")`, assert retained "online", then `machine.systemctl("restart mosquitto.service")` mid-test and assert re-subscribe and availability return — the module-level replay of the two root defects, and the gate that pins the fleet unit shape in one stroke [[nixos-manual]] [[mosquittonix]].

Three developments would legitimately reopen settled questions and deserve standing watch: a merged-and-released upstream reconnect signal (which would let the raw ConnAck match become an event variant and trigger the version bump — but would not change the design, since subscriptions stay application-owned); an incumbent shipping native select controls with state sync or a NixOS service module (go-hass-agent's zero-occurrence record through v14.15.1 is the current evidence against) [[changelogmd]]; and an end-to-end MQTT v5 decision, which loosens the clean-session reasoning and makes message expiry the stale-command cure — the v5 module already ships inside the pinned version [[interim-report-rumqttc-dependency-fitness]].
